options.metric: Annual number of motorist and cyclist deaths
options.reason: Annual counts give the most direct comparison of how many motorist and cyclist deaths were reported each year.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year: motorists ranged from 72 in 2016 to 139 in 2020, while cyclist deaths ranged from 10 in 2018 to 31 in both 2019 and 2023.
options.interpretation: This framing directly answers how many motorist and cyclist deaths occurred year by year, and the chart shows the motorist total was higher in each year. Comparing counts is a defensible direct measure of the annual burden, but it does not express the cyclist deaths as a share of deaths across these two groups.

options.metric: Cyclist and motorist shares of their combined annual deaths
options.denominator: Annual motorist deaths plus annual cyclist deaths
options.reason: The within-year shares show how the relative split between these two road-user groups changes even when their combined totals vary.
options.answer: Cyclists accounted for 9.09% to 27.43% of combined motorist and cyclist deaths, with the minimum in 2013 and maximum in 2019.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how the relative mix of motorist versus cyclist deaths changed year by year, showing cyclist shares ranging from 9.09% to 27.43%. It is defensible for comparing relative proportions across years with different combined totals, but it does not show the absolute number of deaths and its denominator excludes pedestrian deaths.
